FOR campaign/underworld-peoples -- STAGE RED, ONE FAILURE, AND IT IS NOT A PIN TO MOVE. 9e133f78b3a4, gate rc=2 at 184.7s (artifacts and outboard green).

  repl::tests::the_settlements_listing_qualifies_exactly_the_lines_that_would_repeat
  cli/src/repl.rs:679
      left  27
      right 24

READ THOSE TWO NUMBERS BEFORE REACHING FOR A LITERAL: THERE ISN'T ONE. The test computes both sides at runtime:

  let qualified = rendered.iter().zip(&bare)
      .filter(|(line, row)| **line != bare_line(row)).count();

  let in_a_repeating_group = bare.iter()
      .filter(|row| bare.iter().filter(|other| other == row).count() > 1).count();

  assert_eq!(qualified, in_a_repeating_group, "...no more");

So 27 lines came out qualified while only 24 are in a repeating group. The property -- qualify exactly what would repeat, NO MORE -- is violated by three lines. Nothing here drifted; the listing is over-qualifying.

THE MECHANISM I WOULD LOOK AT FIRST, and the test's own comment points at it. Qualification is detected by comparing the rendered line to the bare line it replaced:

  bare_line = "{name} — population {population} — {biome}"

and the comment explains why: "Detected by comparing each rendered line to the bare line it replaced, not by looking for a bracket: the people rung ('Roa of the kobolds') carries no bracket at all."

That detection counts ANY difference from the bare form as qualification. So if your change alters how a rendered line is SPELLED for a reason unrelated to disambiguation -- a people rung that now reads differently, a biome or name string that moved, anything touching that render path -- those lines register as qualified without any disambiguation having occurred. Three lines differing from `bare_line()` for a non-disambiguation reason produces exactly this failure.

You touch domains/species/src/lib.rs and domains/language/src/accession.rs, and the people rung is literally "of the kobolds" -- an underworld people. That is the first place I would look: which three settlements render differently now, and is the difference a bracket-style qualification or a changed people/biome/name string?

IF IT IS THE SECOND, the bug is arguably in the TEST's detection heuristic rather than your code, and the honest fix is to make the test detect qualification structurally rather than by line inequality. But establish which of the two it is before touching either, because the alternative -- that your change really does over-qualify three listings -- is a user-visible defect in the REPL and worth finding.

This is the good kind of red: a test that computes its own expectation cannot go stale, so it is telling you something true about today's tree.
